h1: The 5 Best 56V Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 5 genuine 56V cordless leaf blowers scored on airflow, wet-leaf power and platform, from EGO Power+ at 880 CFM to Echo eFORCE.
summary: The EGO Power+ 880 CFM is the best 56V leaf blower: the strongest airflow here with a 200 MPH turbo. The 765 CFM EGO is the value pick for medium and large yards, and the 615 CFM EGO is the cheapest way into the platform. The Echo eFORCE suits owners already on Echo batteries.
intro: Buying a 56V blower is really choosing a battery family. EGO and Echo both run their outdoor tools on 56V packs, and a blower is often the first purchase before a mower, trimmer or chainsaw joins the garage. Pick the wrong battery now and every later tool costs more or forces a second charger onto the shelf.

That is why this list covers only genuine 56V models and ranks them mostly on airflow in cubic feet per minute, the figure that separates a blower that moves wet leaves from one that merely stirs them. Scores follow spec sheets and yard-owner reports, and we checked each listing for battery and charger details, because a bare tool is not a working blower.

products.name: EGO Power+ Cordless Electric Leaf Blower (880 CFM)
products.verdict: Up to 880 CFM and turbo speeds to 200 MPH. The strongest handheld here.
products.description:
The EGO Power+ 880 CFM handheld delivers up to 880 CFM of air, with turbo speeds up to 200 MPH on the 56V EGO platform. Volume is what moves a wet, matted pile, and 880 CFM gives the headroom to shift leaves that a weaker machine only ruffles. There is no gas, no mixing and no fumes.

It ranks first because it leads the group on airflow. The 765 CFM model gets close for less money, while the Echo eFORCE trails by more than 300 CFM.

Buy it for a large yard and heavy, wet leaf drop. The caveat is price, the highest here, and more power than a small yard needs. Skip it if debris is light, and confirm what is in the box before ordering.
cons: More than a small yard needs
products.idealFor: Large yards and heavy, wet leaf drop.
products.skipIf: You have a small yard or light debris.

products.name: EGO POWER+ Cordless Electric Leaf Blower (765 CFM)
products.verdict: 765 CFM and a 200 MPH turbo, enough for wet leaves at a lower price than the 880.
products.description:
The EGO Power+ 765 CFM blower matches the 880's 200 MPH turbo and the same 56V battery platform, with up to 765 CFM of airflow. That is enough to move wet leaves across a medium or large lawn without gas, and it has a large owner base behind it.

It ranks second since it gives up about 115 CFM to the 880, and it costs more than the 615 CFM model. Against the Echo eFORCE, it moves nearly 240 CFM more.

Buy it for a medium to large yard that wants strong power for less than the flagship. Skip it if you want the absolute maximum airflow. Check the accessories listed with the kit, as the battery and charger are the expensive parts.
products.idealFor: Medium to large yards that want strong power for less.
products.skipIf: You want the absolute maximum airflow.

products.name: EGO POWER+ Cordless Electric Leaf Blower (615 CFM)
products.verdict: 615 CFM covers typical leaf cleanup, and it is the most affordable way into EGO's 56V platform.
products.description:
The EGO Power+ 615 CFM handheld offers up to 615 CFM at the lowest EGO entry price, with no gas and no fumes. It is the cheapest way to join the 56V platform, and 615 CFM covers normal fall cleanup on an average lot.

It ranks third because it struggles with caked wet piles and moves 150 CFM less than the 765. It beats the 530 CFM model by about 85 CFM for modest extra money.

Buy it for an average yard and a dependable first 56V tool. Skip it if you regularly clear wet, matted leaves. If your trees drop heavily, step up to the 765.
products.idealFor: Average yards that want a dependable first 56V tool.
products.skipIf: You regularly clear wet, matted leaves.

products.name: Echo eFORCE 56V 151 MPH 526 CFM Cordless Handheld Blower
products.verdict: 151 MPH and 526 CFM on the Echo eFORCE 56V platform from a pro-focused brand.
products.description:
The Echo eFORCE 56V blower pushes 526 CFM at 151 MPH from a genuine Echo eFORCE battery tool with a pro-focused pedigree, no gas and no maintenance chores. Owners of Echo batteries save money by sharing packs across tools.

It ranks fourth because airflow trails the EGO 765 and 880, and the listing is newer. Platform loyalty is its main argument.

Buy it if you already own Echo eFORCE batteries and tools. Skip it if you are choosing a platform and want maximum airflow. Check what the kit includes, because a bare tool needs a battery and charger.
products.idealFor: Owners of Echo eFORCE batteries and tools.
products.skipIf: You are choosing a platform and want maximum airflow.

products.name: EGO POWER+ Cordless Electric Leaf Blower (530 CFM)
products.verdict: The most modest airflow of the EGO picks, but fine for patios and light leaves.
products.description:
The EGO Power+ 530 CFM handheld is the lightest-duty EGO here, with up to 530 CFM on the 56V platform and a light-duty price. Patios, decks and dry leaves suit it, and it has a long track record on the platform.

It ranks last because 530 CFM is the lowest airflow of the EGO group and weak on wet leaves. It costs less than the others, which explains its place.

Buy it for a small yard and hard surfaces with dry debris. Skip it if your trees drop heavy, wet leaves. Anything over 600 CFM is a better match for real fall cleanup.
pros: Long track record on the platform
cons: Lowest airflow in the EGO group
products.idealFor: Small yards and hard surfaces with dry debris.
products.skipIf: You have trees that drop heavy, wet leaves.

methodology.title: Genuine 56V platform
methodology.description: We only kept blowers that run on a true 56V battery system, because mixing platforms is the most common buying mistake in this category.

methodology.title: Airflow in CFM
methodology.description: Cubic feet per minute was the main ranking input, since it decides whether a blower moves wet material.

methodology.title: Turbo and speed
methodology.description: Air speed in MPH and turbo modes were compared as a second measure of how much work each blower does at the nozzle.

methodology.title: Platform value
methodology.description: We weighed what each battery system offers for future tools, not just the blower itself.

methodology.title: Listing clarity
methodology.description: Listings that make battery and charger inclusion unclear were noted, since some tools ship as bare units.

whatMatters.factor: CFM is the number to read first
whatMatters.detail: CFM measures air volume, and it is what moves a pile of leaves. MPH measures air speed, which helps loosen stuck debris. Wet leaves need high CFM. For a typical yard, 600 to 800 CFM is a comfortable range, and below 550 CFM is for light work only. Find both figures in the title or specs before you order, and compare the same kind of number across brands, since some list peak values.

Some 56V tools are sold bare, with no battery or charger. A blower without a pack is useless on its own, and a battery can cost as much as the tool. Read the listing title and the included items before ordering, and confirm the kit says battery and charger so the total price is not a surprise at checkout.

whatMatters.factor: Pick the platform before the tool
whatMatters.detail: EGO and Echo use different 56V batteries that do not interchange. If you already own one brand's mower or trimmer, buying the same brand's blower lets you share batteries. Starting fresh, EGO has the larger range among the picks here, with four blowers against one Echo, which means more choice in airflow and price as your needs change.

Turbo mode drains a battery fast. A larger amp-hour pack runs longer, but adds weight. If your yard takes 20 minutes, a standard pack suffices. For larger jobs, plan for a bigger pack or a spare, and use turbo only in short bursts for stubborn debris.

A blower you carry for 30 minutes needs to feel balanced. Handheld models vary in weight, and heavier ones tire the wrist. Check the listed weight and the battery's added mass before buying, and note that a higher CFM machine generally weighs more, so match power to the real job rather than buying the biggest number.

faq.q: Are EGO and Echo 56V batteries interchangeable?
faq.a: No. They are separate platforms that share only a voltage label. Buy the blower that matches the batteries you already own, such as the Echo eFORCE for Echo owners and any EGO Power+ model for EGO. Mixing brands means two chargers and two sets of batteries.

faq.q: How many CFM do I need?
faq.a: For a typical yard 600 to 800 CFM is comfortable. Wet leaves call for the 765 or 880 CFM EGO, and light cleanup can use the 530 CFM, which is fine for patios, decks and dry leaves but weak on wet piles.

faq.q: Does the blower come with a battery?
faq.a: Not always. Some 56V tools are sold bare. Read the listing for battery and charger included before you order, since the pack is the costly part of any 56V blower, and a bare tool can double the price.

It boosts airflow temporarily to loosen stubborn debris, but drains the battery faster. Use it in short bursts, such as the 200 MPH turbo on the EGO models, then drop back to normal speed to protect runtime.

faq.q: Can a cordless blower replace a gas one?
faq.a: For most home yards, yes. The 880 CFM EGO Power+ handles wet leaves that used to need gas, without fumes or a pull cord. Very large lots may still want a spare battery or a second pack ready to swap.

faq.q: Is the Echo eFORCE worth buying on its own?
faq.a: Only if you want the Echo platform. On airflow alone it trails the 765 and 880 CFM EGO models by a wide margin, at a similar price tier.

finalTake: The EGO Power+ 880 CFM is the right 56V blower for large yards and wet leaves, with the 765 CFM model the better value for most. Buy the Echo eFORCE only if you already run Echo batteries. Choose the platform first, then the airflow.
